newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on cenbank participation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on cenbank participation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 45 basis points in early trade at 23.65 percent on Friday amid favorable market reaction to Banco de Mexico participation during the prior session, traders said.
"Banco de Mexico capping rates was a very positive move. The market itself is saying so," a trader said.

On Thursday, the central bank drained 9.068 billion pesos in liquidity through three direct sales of government paper and seven repurchase agreements. The bank effectively capped rates by assigning an overnight repurchase agreement at 25.73 percent.
"The market should be quieter today, rates will certainly stay down and dealers will also be watching out a little for what Banco de Mexico does," a money market analyst said.
The analysts also said secondary money market rates had declined on a firm peso. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 0.15 of a centavos firmer at 7.8750/7.8760 per dollar.
"The exchange rate is also responding well," the analyst added.
Overnight rates on bank paper were down 75 basis points at 24.75 percent.
Liquidity of 4.914 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
